hints: Focus on what alkaline hydrolysis does differently from acid hydrolysis, it makes a carboxylate salt plus an alcohol, not a free acid.
Split the ester at the COO link, the left side CH3CH2CO comes from the acid and the right side OCH3 becomes the alcohol.
Match each side to its product, a 3-carbon acid part gives a propanoate salt and a 1-carbon O-CH3 part gives methanol.
walkthrough:
**Recall alkaline hydrolysis**

Think of an ester as acid part joined to alcohol part. Boiling with NaOH breaks it into a sodium carboxylate and an alcohol.

$$\text{ester} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{sodium carboxylate} + \text{alcohol}$$

**Split this ester**

Write the ester to show the split clearly. The left side is the acyl part, the right side is the alkoxy part.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$

**Name the two products**

The left product $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$ has 3 carbons from propanoic acid, so it is sodium propanoate. The right product $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ is methanol.

options.A: Ethanol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with 2 carbons. The alcohol part here is only O-CH3, so it gives methanol with 1 carbon, not ethanol.
options.B: Propan-1-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Students sometimes think the CH3CH2 left side becomes the alcohol, but that side is the acid part and becomes the carboxylate salt.
options.C: Sodium methanoate is $\text{HCO}_2\text{Na}$ with 1 carbon. This swaps the two sides. The 1-carbon side is the alcohol side, not the acid side.
options.D: The acid-derived part is CH3CH2CO, which is propanoate. With NaOH it forms sodium propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, plus methanol.
